name: chengxdadp/tsa-passenger-volume

name: VijayChamakuri/hub-delay-audit
what_it_holds: Auditing minimum-connection-time standards at 15 major US hub airports (SFO, EWR, LGA, ORD, BOS, JFK, LAX, MSP, SLC, SEA, PHX, CLT, DEN, DFW, ATL) using BTS On-Time Performance (Jan 2019, ~584k rows) and DB1B Coupon Survey (Q1 2019, ~9.8M rows) data; analysis.py computes carrier-hub pair statistics across 69 carrier-hub pairs / 5 major carriers (AA, DL, UA, WN, AS), ~91.5% of sample volume. Raw data not committed (download instructions only); single-commit repo.
why_useful: This is the only repo found that actually demonstrates a working BTS T-100/On-Time + DB1B join pipeline end-to-end (download, clean, join, hub-level delay-buffer analysis) — a template for building a fresh, current-quarter T-100/DB1B pull for air-travel-demand cross-checks on ABNB nights (gap 10), even though the committed sample data is limited to Q1 2019.

name: simonpcouch/anyflights
what_it_holds: CRAN-published R package (317 commits) generalizing nycflights13 to any FAA airport/year: get_flights(), get_weather(), get_airports(), get_airlines(), get_planes() pull flight-level departure records (built on underlying FAA/BTS on-time data feeds), hourly weather, and airport/airline/aircraft metadata for a user-specified station+year+month; can bundle results into a data-only R package. Notes FAA usually posts full-year data in Feb/March of the following year (i.e., a lag to be aware of for nowcasting).
why_useful: General-purpose, maintained client for pulling flight-level US air-travel data (a step toward T-100/OTP-style capacity and delay series) by any airport and year, which could be pointed at major leisure gateway airports (MCO, LAS, HNL, MIA) as a demand-kernel proxy alongside TSA throughput; also documents the FAA data-release lag relevant to point-in-time discipline.
time_coverage: Any year/month FAA has published (with ~1 year publication lag noted)
size_hint: Method only; flight-level, so volume scales with airport size
license: CRAN package, MIT-typical (not confirmed in fetch)

name: adsb-tools
